Story & Plot

When seventeen schoolchildren from the same elementary school classroom mysteriously vanish without explanation in the middle of the night at exactly 2:17 AM, a quiet American community is left reeling. Grief and suspicion take over as the town questions who or what is behind the disappearance. The multi-perspective horror narrative spirals around this chilling central mystery, breaking the story up into time-scrambling chapters.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film features dark humor and a surprising amount of wit, balancing sheer dread with moments of levity. Writer-director Zach Cregger hones a blend of unbearable tension and dark humor to a razor-sharp level, recognizing that people on such an intense journey still find room for dark laughs. It enhances the entertainment value by keeping audiences on their toes alongside the suspense.

Performances & Direction

The cast features strong work from Julia Garner, Josh Brolin, Alden Ehrenreich as a cop named Paul, Austin Abrams as a junkie named James, and Benedict Wong as a school principal named Marcus. Reviewers note that every character gets a chance to shine, with all performers bringing their own energy and strong presence to the multi-perspective piece.

Strengths

  • tension-ratcheting construction
  • fascinatingly layered central mystery
  • time-scrambling chapter structure
  • strong ensemble performances
  • sharp blend of horror and dark humor

Weaknesses

While the movie is praised as an instant horror classic, some viewers might find that it functions more as a mystery thriller than a traditional, full-blown horror picture. Additionally, because the narrative relies heavily on a multi-perspective, time-scrambling approach rather than a straightforward point-A-to-point-B path, it requires close attention and may occasionally challenge those looking for a conventional storyline.

Final verdict

Weapons is a shocking, satisfying, and singular horror experience that offers a fresh take on the underbelly of American suburbia. With its razor-sharp direction, fantastic editing, and multi-perspective storytelling, it is an instant classic that is well worth watching.

Story & Plot

A group of young boys and top hotshot kids head to a party at the Cult club expecting a night of fun with music, alcohol, and drugs. Soon, they are locked inside and strangers start to kill the party members one by one in a brutal fight for survival. Satya Nayak must save the day and find out the truth behind the mass killings.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film focuses heavily on high-voltage action, graphic horror, and suspense rather than traditional humor. Entertainment value is derived from the tense single-location premise where characters are forced to play games and face terror.

Performances & Direction

The cast features Vishwak Sen, Gayatri Bhardwaj, Tarak Ponnappa as Elwin, Murali Sharma as the Goa Home Minister, and Srikanth Iyengar. While reviews are sharply divided and the film lacks finesse, the actors carry out this brutal slasher experiment in a contained thriller setting.

Current reviews are sharply divided, with ratings ranging from 1.5/5 to 2.75/5, noting that the slasher thriller is ambitious but lacks finesse. The film settles for convenience when it is expected to push boundaries, and frames the antagonist's motivation as mere vengeance rather than a rebel without a cause.

Final verdict
